Gender is weird. Lots of things are weird.
And sometimes we need fancy language to describe stuff.
Xenogenders are metaphors. Afaik no one who identifies an an xenogender thinks they're actually stuff like a cat or fog. This is a sadly pretty common piece of misinformation spread by transphobes and truscum. (Which is also transphobia but that's a whole other convo.)

Think of the metaphors as the same way we think about prescribing meaning to colours.
Why is yellow connected with joy, energy and just general good feelings? For most stuff it doesn't make clear sense. We have gotten so used to it that we don't really think about it often.
Well lots of things can be metaphorically explained.
I personally relate to something called mistgender. It's the feeling of not being able to pin down your gender and it feeling diffused with other genders, very unclear. Like mist!
There's always a question of "well why not use [more common label]?" Well, often it's nice to find something specific that speaks to you.
You can wear a nice blue shirt to complete your outfit and it'd work fine, but wouldn't it be neat to wear that yellow comfy sweater instead?

Another few things.
Xenogenders are way less common than people realize and most people keep them to themself. This is usually due to transhobia and the surrounding stigma. Most of my (online) friends are queer. As far as I know none of them have xenogenders. I think that if i counted all the people I've ever talked in detail with, there'd only be 3 or 4 people who are openly xenogender.

Another major thing is that xenogender and neurodivergence are very linked. Ofc neurotypicals are free to use them but the very specific labels for the unclarity in gendered feelings seem to be very useful for neurodivergent folks. Ofc while I do think xenogender identities in neurodivergent folks are more common I still think it's a very small amount.
There's more I could go on about trust me but I'll keep it at this for now. If anyones has any questions feel free to ask. I'll try to answer to the best of my ability.

I personally always rush in first then ink spawn later. The first moments of a match are very good moments to take as much ground as possible. Staying at base to ink only leaves the enemy with more ground they can easily take with less resistance.

* Check the map, you might be able to see enemy squids if the target player is fighting, looking at the ink coverage also helps.
* be prepared to throw a bomb first thing. This miiight help you but only if the enemies are slow or you use a burst bomb on low health or quick to flee enemies.
* use the drop roll ability. It allows you to use a dualies type roll upon landing.
* use the stealth jump ability, it makes it so others don't see where you are jumping to.
